title: Hardware throughput matrix & cost-per-token regression harness
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a repeatable, CI-integrated benchmarking harness that runs across a defined hardware matrix (NVIDIA A10, L4, A100, H100) and output standardized tokens/sec and latency (p50/p95/p99) metrics plus cost-per-token reports. The harness should exercise realistic workload profiles (chat streaming, single-turn generation, long-context decoding) and support model variants and quantization profiles. Results will feed a regression detection pipeline that alerts on >5% tokens/sec drop or >10% p95 increase vs baseline and publishes cost-per-token delta compared to reference instance and quantization settings.
acceptance_criteria: Automated job that runs full matrix nightly and on release candidates
Metrics collected: tokens/sec, p50, p95, p99 latency, error rate, GPU utilization, memory headroom
Cost-per-token computed using customer-visible unit costs and instance-hour pricing, exported to dashboard
Regression detector posts GitHub issue and Slack alert when thresholds exceeded
Results stored as time-series and CSV artifacts accessible from perf dashboard and CI jobs
Documentation and runbook for interpreting results and rerunning individual cells
tasks: Design workload profiles (chat short/med/long, single-turn, batch decode) and sample prompts
Implement harness runner that parametrizes: model, quantization, seq_len, batch_size, streaming on/off
Integrate with cluster provisioner to allocate A10/L4/A100/H100 instances with pinned drivers
Collect telemetry: token emit timestamps to compute tokens/sec, per-request latency histograms for p95/p99
Implement cost model: (instance_hourly_cost / (tokens_per_sec * 3600)) and normalize per 1k tokens
Add regression detection logic and thresholds; wire to CI to fail on severe regressions
Create dashboard panels and CSV export; add links in CI job summary
Smoke tests and gating: baseline run, warmup policy, KV cache priming step
implementation_notes: Prefer running using the internal load-tester (perftest) to preserve KV cache semantics; fallback to k6 for HTTP-level smoke checks
Warmup: run a 3-minute priming phase with generated traffic matching production token distribution before measuring
Measure tokens/sec by counting model-token outputs (not bytes) and compute both produced_tokens/sec and consumed_input_tokens/sec
Record GPU power and utilization to help explain cost anomalies; tag runs with driver/cuda/cuDNN versions
We will run each cell multiple times (3 runs) and save median to avoid noisy outliers
For streaming cases compute end-to-end p95 per completed response and per-token emit latency distribution
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: hardware availability across clouds causes noisy comparisons. Mitigation: pin exact instance SKU and profile host image; run same HW in same region where possible
Risk: quantization differences produce non-deterministic outputs that affect token counts. Mitigation: use token-level alignment heuristics and fixed prompts
Risk: cost model drift when cloud prices change. Mitigation: pull pricing from pricing API at job start and store snapshot with results
